section: Educational Psychology · Ch — Cognitive & Social Learning
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student who lacks confidence in solving algebra problems becomes noticeably more confident after watching a classmate of similar ability successfully solve a difficult problem at the board. This boost to self-efficacy, gained by observing a similar peer succeed (rather than succeeding oneself), is called:
explanation: Vicarious experience builds self-efficacy through observing a similar model succeed — its impact is strongest when the observed model is perceived as similar in ability to oneself — distinct from mastery experience (one's own direct success, the strongest source) or verbal persuasion (encouragement from others).
